title: Ensure that authentication is enabled for YCQL interface of the YugabyteDB
description: YCQL authentication is based on roles. Roles can be created with superuser, non- superuser, and login privileges. New roles can be created, and existing ones altered or dropped by administrators using YCQL commands. Reads the YB-TServer GFlags from the web UI at ${YB_TSERVER_WEB:-127.0.0.1:9000}/varz; run it against every TServer. Passes when use_cassandra_authentication=true.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.1 Ensure that authentication is enabled for YCQL interface of the YugabyteDB

audit.command: out=$(curl -sf "http://${YB_TSERVER_WEB:-127.0.0.1:9000}/varz?raw=1" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE -- '--use_cassandra_authentication=(true)([^[:alnum:]_]|$)'; then echo compliant; else echo noncompliant; fi

remediation.command: Add --use_cassandra_authentication=true to every YB-TServer and restart it; then change the default cassandra password (5.2).

title: Ensure that the default password changed for the cassandra role
description: The cassandra role has a default password which must be changed. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Attempts a ycqlsh login as cassandra/cassandra against ${YCQL_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:${YCQL_PORT:-9042} (ycqlsh on PATH); passes only when the server rejects the credentials. A successful login (including with YCQL authentication disabled) fails, an unreachable server fails.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.2 Ensure that the default password changed for the cassandra role

audit.command: command -v ycqlsh >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(ycqlsh -u cassandra -p cassandra -e 'SELECT release_version FROM system.local;' "${YCQL_HOST:-127.0.0.1}" "${YCQL_PORT:-9042}" 2>&1); rc=$?; if [ $rc -eq 0 ]; then echo default_password_accepted; elif printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qiE 'AuthenticationFailed|Bad credentials|incorrect|Unauthorized'; then echo compliant; else exit 1; fi

remediation.command: Log in to ycqlsh as a superuser and run ALTER ROLE cassandra WITH PASSWORD = '<new strong password>';

title: Ensure ysql_enable_auth is set to true
description: The ysql_enable_auth GFlag controls whether password authentication is required for YSQL connections. When set to false (the default), connections are accepted without authentication, which is only appropriate for isolated development environments. In all other environments, this flag must be enabled to enforce password-based access control for the YSQL interface. Reads the YB-TServer GFlags from the web UI at ${YB_TSERVER_WEB:-127.0.0.1:9000}/varz; run it against every TServer. Passes when ysql_enable_auth=true.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.6 Ensure ysql_enable_auth is set to true

audit.command: out=$(curl -sf "http://${YB_TSERVER_WEB:-127.0.0.1:9000}/varz?raw=1" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE -- '--ysql_enable_auth=(true)([^[:alnum:]_]|$)'; then echo compliant; else echo noncompliant; fi

remediation.command: Add --ysql_enable_auth=true to every YB-TServer startup configuration and restart it; then change the default yugabyte password (5.7).

title: Ensure the default password is changed for the yugabyte superuser
description: The yugabyte role is the built-in YSQL superuser in YugabyteDB. By default, it has a well-known password. This default password must be changed before the cluster is deployed to a non-development environment. Leaving the default password in place allows anyone with knowledge of the default to gain full superuser access to all databases in the cluster. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Attempts a ysqlsh login as yugabyte with the default password against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433); passes only when the login is rejected with an authentication error. A successful login (including trust authentication) fails, an unreachable server fails.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.7 Ensure the default password is changed for the yugabyte superuser

audit.command: command -v ysqlsh >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(PGPASSWORD=yugabyte PGPASSFILE=/dev/null ysqlsh -h "${PGHOST:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${PGPORT:-5433}" -U yugabyte -d yugabyte -w -tAc 'SELECT 1' 2>&1); rc=$?; if [ $rc -eq 0 ]; then echo default_password_accepted; elif printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qi 'authentication failed'; then echo compliant; else exit 1; fi

remediation.command: ALTER ROLE yugabyte WITH PASSWORD '<new strong password>'; store it in a password vault, and make sure ysql_enable_auth=true (5.6).

title: Ensure Data Cluster Initialized Successfully
description: First-time installs of YugabyteDB require the instantiation of the database cluster. A database cluster is a collection of databases that are managed by a single server instance. Runs yb-admin -master_addresses ${YB_MASTERS:-127.0.0.1:7100} list_all_masters and list_all_tablet_servers; passes when at least one master and one tablet server are listed and all are ALIVE.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.3 Ensure Data Cluster Initialized Successfully

audit.command: m=${YB_MASTERS:-127.0.0.1:7100}; ms=$(yb-admin -master_addresses "$m" list_all_masters 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; ts=$(yb-admin -master_addresses "$m" list_all_tablet_servers 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; a=$(printf '%s\n' "$ms" | awk 'NR > 1 && NF {n++; if ($0 !~ /ALIVE/) b++} END {print (n > 0 && b == 0) ? "ok" : "bad"}'); t=$(printf '%s\n' "$ts" | awk 'NR > 1 && NF {n++; if ($0 !~ /ALIVE/) b++} END {print (n > 0 && b == 0) ? "ok" : "bad"}'); [ "$a$t" = okok ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.command: Investigate the masters/tablet servers that are not ALIVE (logs under <fs_data_dirs>/yb-data/*/logs) and follow the YugabyteDB troubleshooting guide: https://docs.yugabyte.com/preview/troubleshoot/

title: Ensure latest version of YugabyteDB is installed
description: The YugabyteDB installation version, along with the patches, should be the most recent that is compatible with the organization's operational needs. When obtaining and installing software packages (typically via apt-get or you can compile the source code), it's imperative that packages (or the source code, tarball) are sourced only from valid and authorized repository download.yugabyte.com. Assessed manually here: the benchmark check is environment-specific and cannot be evaluated reliably by a single command.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.5 Ensure latest version of YugabyteDB is installed

audit.command: Run ./bin/yugabyted version (or cat <install dir>/version_metadata.json) on every node and compare with the YugabyteDB release notes. The release series must be supported and on its latest patch build; an old or unsupported version is a finding.

remediation.command: Upgrade to the latest stable version of the YugabyteDB software: Upgrade YB-Master Use the following procedure to upgrade a YB-Master: 1. Stop the older version of the YB-Master process, as follows: pkill yb-master 2. Verify that you are on the directory of the new version, as follows: cd /home/yugabyte/softwareyb-$VER/ 3. Start the newer version of the YB-Master process. For more information, see Start YB-Masters. 4.

title: Ensure the YugabyteDB service is run as a non-root user
description: Though YugabyteDB database may be run as root, it should run as another non-root user. Passes when every running yb-master / yb-tserver process runs as a non-root account (FAIL when none are running).
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.6 Ensure the YugabyteDB service is run as a non-root user

audit.command: out=$(ps -eo user=,comm= 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$2 == "yb-master" || $2 == "yb-tserver" {n++; if ($1 == "root") r++} END {if (n == 0) print "not running"; else if (r > 0) print "root"; else print "compliant"}'

remediation.command: Create a dedicated yugabyte user and group, chown the installation and fs_data_dirs to it and start yb-master/yb-tserver as that user (User=yugabyte in the service unit).

title: Ensure the YugabyteDB Audit Extension (pgAudit) is enabled
description: The YugabyteDB Audit Extension (pgAudit) provides detailed session and/or object audit logging via the standard YugabyteDB logging facility. The goal of pgAudit is to provide YugabyteDB users with the capability to produce audit logs often required to comply with government, financial, or ISO certifications. Runs ysqlsh (add the YugabyteDB bin directory to PATH) against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433) as PGUSER (default yugabyte); supply the password through PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass. Passes when pgaudit is in shared_preload_libraries and pgaudit.log includes at least WRITE, DDL, ROLE and MISC (or ALL).
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.2 Ensure the YugabyteDB Audit Extension (pgAudit) is enabled

audit.command: libs=$(ysqlsh -h "${PGHOST:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${PGPORT:-5433}" -U "${PGUSER:-yugabyte}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-yugabyte}" -tAc "SHOW shared_preload_libraries" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; lg=$(ysqlsh -h "${PGHOST:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${PGPORT:-5433}" -U "${PGUSER:-yugabyte}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-yugabyte}" -tAc "SHOW pgaudit.log" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; case ",$(printf '%s' "$libs" | tr -d ' ')," in *,pgaudit,*) ;; *) echo 'pgaudit not preloaded'; exit 0;; esac; l=$(printf '%s' "$lg" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -d ' '); case ",$l," in *,all,*) echo compliant; exit 0;; esac; for c in write ddl role misc; do case ",$l," in *,$c,*) ;; *) echo "pgaudit.log missing $c"; exit 0;; esac; done; echo compliant

remediation.command: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgaudit; then add --ysql_pg_conf_csv="pgaudit.log='WRITE, DDL, ROLE, MISC',pgaudit.log_level=notice,pgaudit.log_client=ON" to every YB-TServer and restart it.

title: Ensure excessive administrative privileges are revoked
description: With respect to YugabyteDB administrative YSQL commands, only superusers should have elevated privileges. YugabyteDB regular, or application, users should not possess the ability to create roles, create new databases, manage replication, or perform any other action deemed privileged.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 4.2 Ensure excessive administrative privileges are revoked

audit.command: Run ysqlsh -c "\du" and compare each role with the superuser baseline (\du yugabyte). Only approved administrators may hold Superuser, Create role, Create DB, Replication or Bypass RLS; regular or application roles with these attributes are a finding (fix with ALTER ROLE <r> NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEROLE NOCREATEDB NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS).

remediation.command: If any regular or application users have been granted excessive administrative rights, those privileges should be removed immediately via the Yugabyte ALTER ROLE YSQL command. Using the same example above, the following YSQL statements revoke all unnecessary elevated administrative privileges from the regular user appuser: # whoami yugabyte # ysqlsh -c "ALTER ROLE appuser NOSUPERUSER;" ALTER ROLE # ysqlsh -c "ALTER ROLE appuser NOCREATEROLE;" ...

title: Ensure the cassandra and superuser roles are separate
description: The default installation of YugabyteDB includes a superuser role named cassandra. This necessitates the creation of a separate role to be the superuser role. Runs ysqlsh (add the YugabyteDB bin directory to PATH) against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433) as PGUSER (default yugabyte); supply the password through PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Runs ycqlsh against ${YCQL_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:${YCQL_PORT:-9042} with credentials from ~/.cassandra/cqlshrc; passes when the default cassandra role is not a superuser. Also confirm every remaining superuser role is approved.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.3 Ensure the cassandra and superuser roles are separate

audit.command: out=$(ycqlsh -e 'SELECT role FROM system_auth.roles WHERE is_superuser = True;' "${YCQL_HOST:-127.0.0.1}" "${YCQL_PORT:-9042}" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*cassandra[[:space:]]*$' || true

remediation.command: CREATE ROLE <admin> WITH PASSWORD = '<strong>' AND LOGIN = true AND SUPERUSER = true; log in as it and run ALTER ROLE cassandra WITH SUPERUSER = false AND LOGIN = false;

title: Ensure HBA configuration prohibits weak authentication methods
description: The ysql_hba_conf_csv GFlag controls the Host-Based Authentication (HBA) rules for YSQL connections. The authentication methods trust (no password required), md5 (MD5-hashed passwords), and password (cleartext passwords over the wire) are considered weak and should not be used in production environments.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.8 Ensure HBA configuration prohibits weak authentication methods

audit.command: Run SELECT line_number, type, database, user_name, address, auth_method FROM pg_hba_file_rules ORDER BY line_number; FAIL if any reachable row uses md5 or password, or trust (except type local for user yugabyte). The --ysql_hba_conf_csv list should use scram-sha-256/cert and end with a reject catch-all so auto-generated trailing rules are unreachable.

remediation.command: Update the --ysql_hba_conf_csv GFlag so that all reachable entries use strong authentication, and terminate the list with a reject catch-all to neutralize any auto- generated rules: ./bin/yb-tserver \ --ysql_hba_conf_csv='local all yugabyte trust,host all all 0.0.0.0/0 scram- sha-256,host all all ::0/0 scram-sha-256,host all all all reject' Adjust based on your network topology.

title: Ensure password_encryption is set to scram-sha-256
description: The password_encryption parameter controls the algorithm used to hash passwords set by CREATE ROLE and ALTER ROLE statements. When set to md5 or on (which maps to md5), passwords are stored using MD5 which is cryptographically weak. Setting this to scram-sha-256 ensures passwords are stored using SCRAM-SHA-256, which provides strong security against offline password cracking attacks. Runs ysqlsh (add the YugabyteDB bin directory to PATH) against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433) as PGUSER (default yugabyte); supply the password through PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.9 Ensure password_encryption is set to scram-sha-256

audit.command: out=$(ysqlsh -h "${PGHOST:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${PGPORT:-5433}" -U "${PGUSER:-yugabyte}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-yugabyte}" -tAc "SHOW password_encryption" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set it with the YB-TServer GFlag --ysql_pg_conf_csv="password_encryption=scram-sha-256" on every YB-TServer, restart it and reset existing passwords so they are re-hashed with SCRAM.

title: Ensure login via "host" TCP/IP Socket is configured correctly
description: A large number of authentication METHODs are available for hosts connecting using TCP/IP sockets, including: - trust - reject - md5 - scram-sha-256 - password - gss - sspi - ident - pam - ldap - radius - cert METHODs trust, password, and ident are not to be used for remote logins.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 6.2 Ensure login via "host" TCP/IP Socket is configured correctly

audit.command: Test TCP logins: ysqlsh 'host=localhost user=yugabyte sslmode=disable' and 'sslmode=require', then repeat from a remote host. Every host rule in the HBA configuration (--ysql_hba_conf_csv / pg_hba_file_rules) must require a strong method (scram-sha-256 or cert), unencrypted sessions should be rejected (hostssl), and failed attempts must be logged.

remediation.command: Confirm a login attempt has been made by looking for a logged error message detailing the nature of the authenticating failure. In the case of failed login attempts, whether encrypted or unencrypted, check the following: - The server should be sitting on a port exposed to the remote connecting host i.e.

title: Ensure TLS is enabled and configured correctly: server to server
description: YugabyteDB clusters can be configured to use server-to-server encryption to protect data in transit between YugabyteDB servers. When enabled, Transport Layer Security (TLS), the successor to the deprecated Secure Sockets Layer (SSL), is used to ensure data protection for YSQL and YCQL only. Note that there is no planned support for YEDIS. Reads the YB-TServer GFlags from the web UI at ${YB_TSERVER_WEB:-127.0.0.1:9000}/varz; run it against every TServer. Passes when use_node_to_node_encryption=true and allow_insecure_connections=false (the flags the benchmark remediation sets); check the YB-Master web UI (port 7000) the same way. The benchmark audit also expects SHOW ssl to return on.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 7.2 Ensure TLS is enabled and configured correctly: server to server

audit.command: out=$(curl -sf "http://${YB_TSERVER_WEB:-127.0.0.1:9000}/varz?raw=1" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE -- '--use_node_to_node_encryption=(true)([^[:alnum:]_]|$)' && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE -- '--allow_insecure_connections=(false)([^[:alnum:]_]|$)'; then echo compliant; else echo noncompliant; fi

remediation.command: Create node certificates, then start every YB-Master and YB-TServer with --use_node_to_node_encryption=true --allow_insecure_connections=false --certs_dir=<dir> and perform a rolling restart.

title: Ensure TLS is enabled and configured correctly: client to server
description: YugabyteDB clusters can be configured to use client-to-server encryption to protect data in transit between YugabyteDB servers and clients, tools, and APIs. When enabled, Transport Layer Security (TLS), the successor to the deprecated Secure Sockets Layer (SSL), is used to ensure data protection for YSQL and YCQL only. Note that there is no planned support for YEDIS. Runs ysqlsh (add the YugabyteDB bin directory to PATH) against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433) as PGUSER (default yugabyte); supply the password through PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass. Reads the YB-TServer GFlags from the web UI at ${YB_TSERVER_WEB:-127.0.0.1:9000}/varz; run it against every TServer. Passes when YSQL SHOW ssl returns on and the TServer GFlags (from ${YB_TSERVER_WEB:-127.0.0.1:9000}/varz) have use_client_to_server_encryption=true and allow_insecure_connections=false.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 7.3 Ensure TLS is enabled and configured correctly: client to server

audit.command: ssl=$(ysqlsh -h "${PGHOST:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${PGPORT:-5433}" -U "${PGUSER:-yugabyte}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-yugabyte}" -tAc "SHOW ssl" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; out=$(curl -sf "http://${YB_TSERVER_WEB:-127.0.0.1:9000}/varz?raw=1" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; if [ "$ssl" = on ] && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE -- '--use_client_to_server_encryption=true([^[:alnum:]_]|$)' && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE -- '--allow_insecure_connections=false([^[:alnum:]_]|$)'; then echo compliant; else echo noncompliant; fi

remediation.command: Start every YB-TServer with --use_client_to_server_encryption=true --allow_insecure_connections=false --certs_for_client_dir=<dir> (rolling restart) and configure clients with sslmode=verify-full / YCQL TLS.

title: Ensure base backups are configured and functional
description: Backup and restoration is the process of creating and storing copies of your data for protection against data loss. With a proper backup strategy, you can always restore your data to a most-recent known working state and minimize application downtime. This in turn guarantees business and application continuity.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 8.1 Ensure base backups are configured and functional

audit.command: Run yb-admin -master_addresses <masters> list_snapshot_schedules: at least one active schedule must exist. Run yb-admin -master_addresses <masters> list_snapshots: the most recent snapshot of each schedule must be COMPLETE (FAILED or CREATING, or no COMPLETE snapshot, is a finding). Confirm snapshots are also exported off-cluster and restores are tested.

remediation.command: Using distributed snapshots allows you to back up a database and then restore it in case of a software or operational error, with minimal recovery time objectives (RTO) and overhead. To back up a database, create a snapshot using the create_database_snapshot command, as follows: ./bin/yb-admin -master_addresses <ip1:7100,ip2:7100,ip3:7100> create_database_snapshot ysql.<database_name> A unique ID for the snapshot is returned, as shown in the ...

title: Ensure packages are obtained from authorized repositories
description: Standard Linux distributions, although possessing the requisite packages, often do not have YugabyteDB pre-installed. The installation process includes installing the binaries and the means to generate a data cluster. Package installation should include both the server and client packages. Contribution modules are optional depending upon one's architectural requirements (they are recommended though).
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.1 Ensure packages are obtained from authorized repositories

audit.command: Inspect the configured package repositories and download sources: YugabyteDB packages must come only from software.yugabyte.com (or an approved internal mirror of it). Verify each installation archive against the published checksum (e.g. sha1sum <archive> compared with <archive URL>.sha); any other source or a mismatch is a finding.

remediation.command: Alter the configured repositories so they only include valid and authorized sources of packages. #!/bin/bash # URL of the file to download FILE_URL="https://software.yugabyte.com/releases/2025.2.4.0/yugabyte- 2025.2.4.0-b122-linux-x86_64.tar.gz" # Download the file wget $FILE_URL

title: Ensure a separate user and group exist for YugabyteDB
description: Create separate userid and group for YugabyteDB. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when the yugabyte group and user exist and the user is a member of the group.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.4 Ensure a separate user and group exist for YugabyteDB

audit.command: g=$(getent group yugabyte) || exit 1; u=$(getent passwd yugabyte) || exit 1; gid=$(printf '%s' "$g" | cut -d: -f3); ugid=$(printf '%s' "$u" | cut -d: -f4); members=$(printf '%s' "$g" | cut -d: -f4); if [ "$gid" = "$ugid" ] || printf '%s' ",$members," | grep -q ',yugabyte,'; then echo compliant; else echo 'user not in group'; fi

remediation.command: groupadd yugabyte; useradd -m -d /home/yugabyte -s /bin/bash -g yugabyte -u <UID> yugabyte (use an unused UID).

title: Ensure clocks are synchronized on all nodes
description: Enabling Network Time Protocol (NTP), or some equivalent way, to keep clocks on all nodes in sync is critical. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Uses timedatectl (systemd); passes when the clock is reported as NTP-synchronised by chronyd, ntpd or systemd-timesyncd.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.7 Ensure clocks are synchronized on all nodes

audit.command: out=$(timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized --value 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Install and enable chrony (or ntpd) on every node in the cluster, pointing all nodes at the same time sources: systemctl enable --now chronyd.

title: Ensure the file permissions mask is correct
description: Files are always created using a default set of permissions. File permissions can be restricted by applying a permissions mask called the umask. The yugabyte user account should use a umask of 077 to deny file access to all user accounts except the owner.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 2.1 Ensure the file permissions mask is correct

audit.command: As root run su - yugabyte -c umask. The umask of the yugabyte user must be 0077 or more restrictive; anything less restrictive (e.g. the default 0022) is a finding. Check .bash_profile, .profile and .bashrc of the yugabyte user.

remediation.command: Depending upon the yugabyte user's environment, the umask is typically set in the initialization file .bash_profile, but may also be set in .profile or .bashrc. To set the umask, add the following to the appropriate profile file: # whoami yugabyte # cd ~ # ls -ld .{bash_profile,profile,bashrc} ls: cannot access '.bash_profile': No such file or directory ls: cannot access '.profile': No such file or directory ls: cannot access '.bashrc': No such ...

title: Ensure the log destinations are set correctly
description: YugabyteDB by default supports logging server messages to stderr. Assessed manually here: the benchmark check is environment-specific and cannot be evaluated reliably by a single command.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.1 Ensure the log destinations are set correctly

audit.command: Run SHOW log_destination; in ysqlsh. The value (default stderr) must include every log destination your organisation logging policy requires (e.g. stderr, csvlog, syslog). Missing required destinations are a finding.

remediation.command: Use the yb-tserver binary and its flags to configure the YB-TServer server. Add the following GFLAG to YB-TServer: ./bin/yb-tserver --ysql_pg_conf_csv="log_destination='stderr'"

title: Ensure the log file permissions are set correctly
description: The log_file_mode setting determines the file permissions for log files when logging_collector is enabled. The parameter value is expected to be a numeric mode specification in the form accepted by the chmod and umask system calls. (To use the customary octal format, the number must start with a 0) The permissions should be set to allow only the necessary access to authorized personnel. Runs ysqlsh (add the YugabyteDB bin directory to PATH) against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433) as PGUSER (default yugabyte); supply the password through PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass. Passes when log_file_mode grants no access to other users (default 0600; 0640/0660 only if your policy allows group access).
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.3 Ensure the log file permissions are set correctly

audit.command: out=$(ysqlsh -h "${PGHOST:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${PGPORT:-5433}" -U "${PGUSER:-yugabyte}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-yugabyte}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN right(current_setting('log_file_mode'), 1) = '0' THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'mode ' || current_setting('log_file_mode') END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set it with the YB-TServer GFlag --ysql_pg_conf_csv="log_file_mode='0600'" on every YB-TServer and restart it.

title: Ensure the correct messages are written to the server log
description: The log_min_messages setting specifies the message levels that are written to the server log. Each level includes all the levels that follow it. The lower the level (vertically, below), the fewer messages are sent. Runs ysqlsh (add the YugabyteDB bin directory to PATH) against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433) as PGUSER (default yugabyte); supply the password through PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass. Passes when log_min_messages is warning or more verbose.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.11 Ensure the correct messages are written to the server log

audit.command: out=$(ysqlsh -h "${PGHOST:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${PGPORT:-5433}" -U "${PGUSER:-yugabyte}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-yugabyte}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN lower(current_setting('log_min_messages')) IN ('debug5','debug4','debug3','debug2','debug1','info','notice','warning') THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set it with the YB-TServer GFlag --ysql_pg_conf_csv="log_min_messages='warning'" on every YB-TServer and restart it.

title: Ensure the correct YSQL statements generating errors are recorded
description: The log_min_error_statement setting causes all YSQL statements generating errors at or above the specified severity level to be recorded in the server log. Each level includes all the levels that follow it. The lower the level (vertically, below), the fewer messages are recorded. Runs ysqlsh (add the YugabyteDB bin directory to PATH) against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433) as PGUSER (default yugabyte); supply the password through PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass. Passes when log_min_error_statement is error or more verbose.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.12 Ensure the correct YSQL statements generating errors are recorded

audit.command: out=$(ysqlsh -h "${PGHOST:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${PGPORT:-5433}" -U "${PGUSER:-yugabyte}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-yugabyte}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN lower(current_setting('log_min_error_statement')) IN ('debug5','debug4','debug3','debug2','debug1','info','notice','warning','error') THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set it with the YB-TServer GFlag --ysql_pg_conf_csv="log_min_error_statement='error'" on every YB-TServer and restart it.

title: Ensure 'log_connections' is enabled
description: Enabling the log_connections setting causes each attempted connection to the server to be logged, as well as successful completion of client authentication. This parameter cannot be changed after the session start. Runs ysqlsh (add the YugabyteDB bin directory to PATH) against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433) as PGUSER (default yugabyte); supply the password through PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.17 Ensure 'log_connections' is enabled

audit.command: out=$(ysqlsh -h "${PGHOST:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${PGPORT:-5433}" -U "${PGUSER:-yugabyte}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-yugabyte}" -tAc "SHOW log_connections" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set it with the YB-TServer GFlag --ysql_pg_conf_csv="log_connections='on'" on every YB-TServer and restart it.

title: Ensure 'log_disconnections' is enabled
description: Enabling the log_disconnections setting logs the end of each session, including session duration. This parameter cannot be changed after the session start. Runs ysqlsh (add the YugabyteDB bin directory to PATH) against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433) as PGUSER (default yugabyte); supply the password through PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.18 Ensure 'log_disconnections' is enabled

audit.command: out=$(ysqlsh -h "${PGHOST:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${PGPORT:-5433}" -U "${PGUSER:-yugabyte}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-yugabyte}" -tAc "SHOW log_disconnections" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set it with the YB-TServer GFlag --ysql_pg_conf_csv="log_disconnections='on'" on every YB-TServer and restart it.

title: Ensure 'log_line_prefix' is set correctly
description: The log_line_prefix setting specifies a printf-style string that is prefixed to each logline. If blank, no prefix is used. You should configure this as recommended by the pgBadger development team unless directed otherwise by your organization's logging policy. % characters begin "escape sequences" that are replaced with status information as outlined below. Unrecognized escapes are ignored. Runs ysqlsh (add the YugabyteDB bin directory to PATH) against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433) as PGUSER (default yugabyte); supply the password through PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass. Passes when log_line_prefix contains every escape of the minimum '%m [%p]: [%l-1] db=%d,user=%u,app=%a,client=%h' (%m %p %l %d %u %a %h).
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.21 Ensure 'log_line_prefix' is set correctly

audit.command: out=$(ysqlsh -h "${PGHOST:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${PGPORT:-5433}" -U "${PGUSER:-yugabyte}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-yugabyte}" -tAc "SHOW log_line_prefix" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; for t in '%m' '%p' '%l' '%d' '%u' '%a' '%h'; do case "$out" in *"$t"*) ;; *) echo "missing $t"; exit 0;; esac; done; echo compliant

remediation.command: Set it with the YB-TServer GFlag --ysql_pg_conf_csv="\"log_line_prefix='%m [%p]: [%l-1] db=%d,user=%u,app=%a,client=%h '\"" on every YB-TServer and restart it.

title: Ensure 'log_statement' is set correctly
description: The log_statement setting specifies the types of YSQL statements that are logged. Valid values are: - none - ddl - mod - all It is recommended this be set to ddl unless otherwise directed by your organization's logging policy. Runs ysqlsh (add the YugabyteDB bin directory to PATH) against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433) as PGUSER (default yugabyte); supply the password through PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass. Passes when log_statement is ddl, mod or all (anything but none).
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.22 Ensure 'log_statement' is set correctly

audit.command: out=$(ysqlsh -h "${PGHOST:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${PGPORT:-5433}" -U "${PGUSER:-yugabyte}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-yugabyte}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN current_setting('log_statement') <> 'none' THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'none' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set it with the YB-TServer GFlag --ysql_pg_conf_csv="log_statement='ddl'" on every YB-TServer and restart it.

title: Ensure that auditing is enabled for YCQL
description: Audit logging can be used to record information about YCQL statements or events (such as login events) and log the records on a per-node basis into the YB-Tserver logs. Audit logging can be enabled on YugabyteDB cluster by setting the ycql_enable_audit_log TServer flag to true. By default, each TServer records all login events and YCQL commands issued to the server. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Reads the YB-TServer GFlags from the web UI at ${YB_TSERVER_WEB:-127.0.0.1:9000}/varz; run it against every TServer. Passes when ycql_enable_audit_log=true.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.3 Ensure that auditing is enabled for YCQL

audit.command: out=$(curl -sf "http://${YB_TSERVER_WEB:-127.0.0.1:9000}/varz?raw=1" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE -- '--ycql_enable_audit_log=(true)([^[:alnum:]_]|$)'; then echo compliant; else echo noncompliant; fi

remediation.command: Add --ycql_enable_audit_log=true to every YB-TServer and restart it.

title: Ensure sudo is configured correctly
description: It is common to have more than one authorized individual administering the YugabyteDB service at the Operating System level. It is also quite common to permit login privileges to individuals on a YugabyteDB host who otherwise are not authorized to access the server's data cluster and files.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 4.1 Ensure sudo is configured correctly

audit.command: Review /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d: escalation to the yugabyte account must be granted only to an approved DBA group (e.g. %dba ALL= /bin/su - yugabyte, file mode 600). As a non-member run sudo su - yugabyte (must be refused) and as a DBA group member confirm it succeeds; any broader grant is a finding.

remediation.command: As superuser root, execute the following commands: # echo '%dba ALL= /bin/su - yugabyte' > /etc/sudoers.d/yugabyte # chmod 600 /etc/sudoers.d/yugabyte This grants any Operating System user that is a member of the dba group to use sudo su - yugabyte to become the yugabyte user. Ensure that all Operating System user's that need such access are members of the group.

title: Ensure excessive function privileges are revoked
description: In certain situations, to provide the required functionality, YugabyteDB needs to execute internal logic (stored procedures, functions, triggers, etc.) and/or external code modules with elevated privileges. However, if the privileges required for execution are at a higher level than the privileges assigned to organizational users invoking the functionality applications/programs, those users are indirectly provided ... Assessed manually here: the benchmark check is environment-specific and cannot be evaluated reliably by a single command.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 4.3 Ensure excessive function privileges are revoked

audit.command: Run SELECT nspname, proname, prosecdef, rolname, proconfig FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON p.pronamespace = n.oid JOIN pg_authid a ON a.oid = p.proowner WHERE prosecdef OR NOT proconfig IS NULL; Every SECURITY DEFINER function (prosecdef = t) must be justified, owned by an appropriate role and have a fixed search_path; unjustified ones are a finding.

remediation.command: Where possible, revoke SECURITY DEFINER on YugabyteDB functions. To change a SECURITY DEFINER function to SECURITY INVOKER, run the following YSQL: # whoami root # sudo su - yugabyte # ysqlsh -c "ALTER FUNCTION [functionname] SECURITY INVOKER;" If it is not possible to revoke SECURITY DEFINER, ensure the function can be executed by only the accounts that absolutely need such functionality: yugabyte=# SELECT proname, proacl FROM pg_proc WHERE ...

title: Ensure excessive DML privileges are revoked
description: DML (insert, update, delete) operations at the table level should be restricted to only authorized users. YugabyteDB manages table-level DML permissions via the GRANT statement.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 4.4 Ensure excessive DML privileges are revoked

audit.command: In each database list users (\du+ *) and tables (\dt *.*) and review table grants (\dp or information_schema.role_table_grants). Any user holding INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE on tables it does not need for its role is a finding; revoke with REVOKE <priv> ON <table> FROM <user>.

remediation.command: If a given database user has been granted excessive DML privileges for a given database table, those privileges should be revoked immediately using the REVOKE YSQL command. Continuing with the example above, remove unauthorized grants for appreader user using the REVOKE statement and verify the Boolean values are now false. yugabyte=# REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLE customer FROM appreader;

title: Ensure Row Level Security (RLS) is configured correctly
description: In addition to the YSQL-standard privilege system available through GRANT, tables can have row security policies that restrict, on a per-user basis, which individual rows can be returned by normal queries or inserted, updated, or deleted by data modification commands. This feature is also known as Row Level Security (RLS).
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 4.5 Ensure Row Level Security (RLS) is configured correctly

audit.command: Identify the tables that require row-level security under business policy, then run SELECT oid, relname, relrowsecurity FROM pg_class WHERE relrowsecurity IS TRUE; and review policies with SELECT * FROM pg_policies; Any table that should be RLS-protected but is missing, or whose policies do not restrict rows as intended, is a finding.

remediation.command: In this example, we are using the using the example passwd table. We will create three database roles to illustrate the workings of RLS: yugabyte=# CREATE ROLE admin; CREATE ROLE yugabyte=# CREATE ROLE bob; CREATE ROLE yugabyte=# CREATE ROLE alice; CREATE ROLE Now, we will insert known data into the passwd table: yugabyte=# INSERT INTO passwd VALUES ('admin','xxx',0,0,'Admin','111-222-3333',null,'/root','/bin/dash');

title: Ensure there are no unnecessary roles or excessive privileges
description: Verify each role is required and has only the privileges needed to do its job.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.4 Ensure there are no unnecessary roles or excessive privileges

audit.command: As a YCQL superuser run SELECT role, can_login, is_superuser, member_of FROM system_auth.roles; and SELECT * FROM system_auth.role_permissions; Any role that is not needed, or any role holding more permissions than its function requires, is a finding (DROP ROLE / REVOKE ... FROM ...).

remediation.command: Remove any unnecessary roles and/or permissions in accordance with organizational needs. Drop unnecessary roles by issuing the following command: cassandra@ycqlsh> DROP ROLE IF EXISTS developer Alternatively, you can revoke permissions. For example, you can revoke the engineering role from the user john as follows: cassandra@ycqlsh> REVOKE engineering FROM john;

title: Ensure that YCQL only listens for network connections on authorized interfaces
description: The cql_proxy_bind_address GFLAG setting specifies the IP address and port for YCQL interface. cql_proxy_bind_address should be set according to your organization's approved IP address and ports policy.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.5 Ensure that YCQL only listens for network connections on authorized interfaces

audit.command: Check the cql_proxy_bind_address GFlag of every YB-TServer (curl -s http://<tserver>:9000/varz | grep cql_proxy_bind_address, or the tserver flag file). It must name an authorised address and port, not 0.0.0.0 or an unapproved interface.

remediation.command: Use the yb-tserver binary and its flags to configure the YB-TServer server. Add the following GFLAG to YB-TServer: ./bin/yb-tserver --cql_proxy_bind_address <ip address>:<port>

title: Ensure login via "local" UNIX Domain Socket is configured correctly
description: A remote host login, via SSH, is arguably the most secure means of remotely accessing and administering the YugabyteDB server. Once connected to the YugabyteDB server, using the ysqlsh client, via UNIX DOMAIN SOCKETS, while using the peer authentication method is the most secure mechanism available for local database connections.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 6.1 Ensure login via "local" UNIX Domain Socket is configured correctly

audit.command: As the yugabyte OS user run ./bin/ysqlsh -U yugabyte -d yugabyte (should succeed), then as another OS user (su - user1) run the same command: it must fail (e.g. Peer authentication failed). Review local rules in --ysql_hba_conf_csv / pg_hba_file_rules: no trust for local connections other than the intended superuser path.

remediation.command: Creation of a database account that matches the local account allows PEER authentication: # ./bin/ysqlsh -c "CREATE ROLE user1 WITH LOGIN;" CREATE ROLE Execute the following as the UNIX user account, the default authentication rules should now permit the login: # su - user1 # whoami user1 # ./bin/ysqlsh -d yugabyte yugabyte=# As per the host-based authentication rules in $PGDATA/pg_hba.conf, all login attempts via UNIX DOMAIN SOCKETS are ...

title: Ensure security-relevant runtime GFlags are configured correctly
description: YugabyteDB exposes runtime parameters across five context levels: backend, postmaster, sighup, superuser, and user. Unauthorized or misconfigured settings at these levels can enable denial of service, information disclosure, audit evasion, or privilege escalation.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 7.1 Ensure security-relevant runtime GFlags are configured correctly

audit.command: Run SELECT name, setting, context FROM pg_settings WHERE name IN ('ignore_system_indexes','jit_debugging_support','jit_profiling_support','log_connections','log_disconnections','allow_system_table_mods','logging_collector','shared_preload_libraries','password_encryption','ssl','log_hostname','log_line_prefix','log_statement','log_error_verbosity','session_preload_libraries','local_preload_libraries') ORDER BY name; and compare each value with the benchmark reference table.

remediation.command: Set all required parameters in a single --ysql_pg_conf_csv GFlag on every YB-TServer. The flag may be specified only once per process; if it is repeated, only the last occurrence takes effect. Entries whose values contain commas (such as log_line_prefix) must be enclosed in double quotes per the flag's CSV format.

title: Ensure the pgcrypto extension is installed and configured correctly
description: YugabyteDB must implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure or modification of organization-defined information at rest (to include, at a minimum, PII and classified information) on organization-defined information system components.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 7.4 Ensure the pgcrypto extension is installed and configured correctly

audit.command: Run SELECT * FROM pg_available_extensions WHERE name = 'pgcrypto'; and, in each database holding sensitive data, SELECT * FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'pgcrypto'; If data requires column encryption and pgcrypto is not installed or used, this is a finding; also confirm disk/filesystem encryption where policy requires it.

remediation.command: The pgcrypto extension is included with the YugabyteDB 'contrib' package. Although included, it needs to be created in the database. As the database administrator, run the following: yugabyte=# CREATE EXTENSION pgcrypto; Verify pgcrypto is installed: yugabyte=# SELECT * FROM pg_available_extensions WHERE name='pgcrypto';

title: Ensure systemd Service Files Are Enabled
description: Confirm, and correct if necessary, the YugabyteDB systemd service is enabled.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.2 Ensure systemd Service Files Are Enabled

audit.command: Run systemctl get-default and systemctl list-dependencies <default target> | grep -i yugabyte. The YugabyteDB service (e.g. yugabyted.service, or yb-master/yb-tserver units) must be enabled as a want of the default target and run as the dedicated user with Restart=on-failure.

remediation.command: Irrespective of package source, YugabyteDB services can be identified because it typically includes the text string "yugabyted". PGDG installs do not automatically register the service as a "want" of the default systemd target. Multiple instances of YugabyteDB services often distinguish themselves using a version number.

title: Ensure the filename pattern for log files is set correctly
description: The log_filename setting specifies the filename pattern for log files. The value for log_filename should match your organization's logging policy. The value is treated as a strftime pattern, so %-escapes can be used to specify time- varying file names. The supported %-escapes are similar to those listed in the Open Group's strftime specification. Assessed manually here: the benchmark check is environment-specific and cannot be evaluated reliably by a single command.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.2 Ensure the filename pattern for log files is set correctly

audit.command: Run SHOW log_filename; in ysqlsh (default postgresql-%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S.log). The pattern must match your organisation log naming and retention policy (for example postgresql-%a.log for a weekly rotation set).

remediation.command: Use the yb-tserver binary and its flags to configure the YB-TServer server. Add the following GFLAG to YB-TServer: ./bin/yb-tserver --ysql_pg_conf_csv="log_filename='postgresql-%a.log'"

title: Ensure 'log_truncate_on_rotation' is enabled
description: Enabling the log_truncate_on_rotation setting when logging_collector is enabled causes YugabyteDB to truncate (overwrite) existing log files with the same name during log rotation instead of appending to them. Note: Truncation will occur only when a new file is being opened due to time-based rotation, not during server startup or size-based rotation (see later in this benchmark for size-based rotation details). Runs ysqlsh (add the YugabyteDB bin directory to PATH) against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433) as PGUSER (default yugabyte); supply the password through PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.4 Ensure 'log_truncate_on_rotation' is enabled

audit.command: out=$(ysqlsh -h "${PGHOST:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${PGPORT:-5433}" -U "${PGUSER:-yugabyte}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-yugabyte}" -tAc "SHOW log_truncate_on_rotation" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set it with the YB-TServer GFlag --ysql_pg_conf_csv="log_truncate_on_rotation='on'" on every YB-TServer and restart it.

title: Ensure the maximum log file lifetime is set correctly
description: When logging_collector is enabled, the log_rotation_age parameter determines the maximum lifetime of an individual log file (depending on the value of log_filename). After this many minutes have elapsed, a new log file will be created via automatic log file rotation. Current best practices advise log rotation at least daily, but your organization's logging policy should dictate your rotation schedule. Runs ysqlsh (add the YugabyteDB bin directory to PATH) against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433) as PGUSER (default yugabyte); supply the password through PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass. Passes when time-based rotation is enabled (log_rotation_age > 0, default 1d); confirm the value matches the logging policy.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.5 Ensure the maximum log file lifetime is set correctly

audit.command: out=$(ysqlsh -h "${PGHOST:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${PGPORT:-5433}" -U "${PGUSER:-yugabyte}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-yugabyte}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN setting::bigint > 0 THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'disabled' END FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'log_rotation_age'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set it with the YB-TServer GFlag --ysql_pg_conf_csv="log_rotation_age='1d'" (or the value your policy requires) on every YB-TServer and restart it.

title: Ensure the maximum log file size is set correctly
description: The log_rotation_size setting determines the maximum size of an individual log file. Once the maximum size is reached, automatic log file rotation will occur. Runs ysqlsh (add the YugabyteDB bin directory to PATH) against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433) as PGUSER (default yugabyte); supply the password through PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass. Passes when size-based rotation is enabled (log_rotation_size > 0, default 10MB); confirm the value matches the logging policy.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.6 Ensure the maximum log file size is set correctly

audit.command: out=$(ysqlsh -h "${PGHOST:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${PGPORT:-5433}" -U "${PGUSER:-yugabyte}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-yugabyte}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN setting::bigint > 0 THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'disabled' END FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'log_rotation_size'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set it with the YB-TServer GFlag --ysql_pg_conf_csv="log_rotation_size='1GB'" (or the value your policy requires) on every YB-TServer and restart it.

title: Ensure the correct syslog facility is selected
description: The syslog_facility setting specifies the syslog "facility" to be used when logging to syslog is enabled. You can choose from any of the 'local' facilities: - LOCAL0 - LOCAL1 - LOCAL2 - LOCAL3 - LOCAL4 - LOCAL5 - LOCAL6 - LOCAL7 Your organization's logging policy should dictate which facility to use based on the syslog daemon in use.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.7 Ensure the correct syslog facility is selected

audit.command: Run SHOW syslog_facility; in ysqlsh (default local0). Where syslog is a log destination, the facility must be the one your syslog configuration routes to the protected YugabyteDB log (for example local1); an unrouted or shared facility is a finding.

remediation.command: Use the yb-tserver binary and its flags to configure the YB-TServer server (in this example, setting it to the LOCAL1 facility). Add the following GFLAG to YB- TServer: ./bin/yb-tserver --ysql_pg_conf_csv="syslog_facility='local1'"

title: Ensure syslog messages are not suppressed
description: When logging to Syslog and this is on, then each message will be prefixed by an increasing sequence number.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.8 Ensure syslog messages are not suppressed

audit.command: Run SHOW syslog_sequence_numbers; in ysqlsh. Where syslog is a log destination it must be on (the default), so that repeated messages are not suppressed by the syslog daemon; off is a finding.

remediation.command: Set it with the YB-TServer GFlag --ysql_pg_conf_csv="syslog_sequence_numbers='on'" on every YB-TServer and restart it.

title: Ensure syslog messages are not lost due to size
description: YugabyteDB log messages can exceed 1024 bytes, which is a typical size limit for traditional Syslog implementations. When syslog_split_messages is off, YugabyteDB server log messages are delivered to the Syslog service as is, and it is up to the Syslog service to cope with the potentially bulky messages.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.9 Ensure syslog messages are not lost due to size

audit.command: Run SHOW syslog_split_messages; in ysqlsh. Where syslog is a log destination it must be on (the default), so that messages longer than about 1024 bytes are split instead of truncated or lost; off is a finding.

remediation.command: Use the yb-tserver binary and its flags to configure the YB-TServer server. Add the following GFLAG to YB-TServer: ./bin/yb-tserver --ysql_pg_conf_csv="syslog_split_messages='on'"

title: Ensure the program name for YugabyteDB syslog messages is correct
description: The syslog_ident setting specifies the program name used to identify YugabyteDB messages in syslog logs. An example of a possible program name is yugabyte. Assessed manually here: the benchmark check is environment-specific and cannot be evaluated reliably by a single command.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.10 Ensure the program name for YugabyteDB syslog messages is correct

audit.command: Run SHOW syslog_ident; in ysqlsh (default postgres). The program name must match the value your syslog routing and SIEM rules expect for YugabyteDB (for example yugabyte); a value that does not match the logging policy is a finding.

remediation.command: Use the yb-tserver binary and its flags to configure the YB-TServer server (in this example, assuming a program name of yugabyte). Add the following GFLAG to YB- TServer: ./bin/yb-tserver --ysql_pg_conf_csv="syslog_ident='yugabyte'"

title: Ensure 'debug_print_parse' is disabled
description: The debug_print_parse setting enables printing the resulting parse tree for each executed query. These messages are emitted at the LOG message level. Unless directed otherwise by your organization's logging policy, it is recommended this setting be disabled by setting it to off. Runs ysqlsh (add the YugabyteDB bin directory to PATH) against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433) as PGUSER (default yugabyte); supply the password through PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass.
reference: CIS YugabyteDB Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1.13 Ensure 'debug_print_parse' is disabled

audit.command: out=$(ysqlsh -h "${PGHOST:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${PGPORT:-5433}" -U "${PGUSER:-yugabyte}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-yugabyte}" -tAc "SHOW debug_print_parse" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set it with the YB-TServer GFlag --ysql_pg_conf_csv="debug_print_parse='off'" on every YB-TServer and restart it.

title: Ensure 'debug_print_rewritten' is disabled
description: The debug_print_rewritten setting enables printing the query rewriter output for each executed query. These messages are emitted at the LOG message level. Unless directed otherwise by your organization's logging policy, it is recommended this setting be disabled by setting it to off. Runs ysqlsh (add the YugabyteDB bin directory to PATH) against PGHOST/PGPORT (default 127.0.0.1:5433) as PGUSER (default yugabyte); supply the password through PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass.

TERSE excludes the logging of DETAIL, HINT, QUERY, and CONTEXT error information.
